_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Accounting P2 (Managerial Accounting and Bookkeeping), November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The optional
'information' field (array of lines) carries the INFORMATION block of each main question; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that main question and applies to all of its sub-questions.
The pre-printed ANSWER BOOK (paper2_answer_book.pdf) is tracked beside the paper.
memo_answer reproduces the marking guideline's figures and workings line by line (tick marks
removed; marking notes such as 'one part correct' kept). Unnumbered bullet sub-parts of a
question are kept in one entry with their marks added.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Periodic System, VAT and Fixed Assets 35 marks 30 min; Q2 Budgeting
35 marks 30 min; Q3 Cost Accounting 40 marks 30 min; Q4 Reconciliations 40 marks 30 min. A Grade 11
Financial Indicator Formula Sheet is attached to the paper (not transcribed here). Ledger accounts in
the memo are written one line per entry as 'Date Details Amount' (debit side first, then credit side).

questions.context: 1.2 VAT INFORMATION: Siyanda Traders is a VAT-registered business. The VAT rate is 15%. The following transactions took place in May 2025: (i) Cash sales of goods: R11 500 (VAT included) (ii) Credit purchase of goods: R6 900 (VAT excluded) (iii) Purchase of a motor car for the owner’s personal use: R450 000 (VAT included) (iv) Paid for repairs to the delivery vehicle: VAT: R225 REQUIRED:
questions.text: Calculate the VAT amount included in the cash sales.
Calculate the input VAT Siyanda Traders may claim.
Why can VAT not be claimed on the purchase of the vehicle?
questions.memo_answer:
Any ONE explanation
• A motor car was bought for the owner’s personal use, not for business purposes.
• Motor cars acquired for private use (such as for the owner’s personal use) are specifically excluded from input VAT claims, even if VAT was paid on the purchase.
• The vehicle is not being used to generate income for the business; the
VAT is not deductible.

questions.text: Give ONE reason why it is important for a business to keep proper VAT records.
questions.memo_answer:
Any valid reason
• Legal requirement/comply with SARS regulations
• Accurate VAT returns/ensures correct VAT is paid or claimed
• Avoid penalties/prevents fines and interest from SARS
• Proof of VAT transactions
• Better control of business finances
• To identify mistakes in VAT calculations
• Ensures proper VAT reconciliation

questions.text: Explain ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of being a VAT- registered business.
questions.memo_answer:
ADVANTAGE (any one): Can claim input VAT / Creates business credibility / Required for larger businesses (turnover > R1 million) / Eligible for VAT refunds / Improves financial record-keeping
DISADVANTAGE (any one): More admin and paperwork / Penalties if VAT is not paid on time / Need to charge customers VAT / Risk of audits by SARS / Can be costly for small businesses

• Automated data entry – Fewer errors

• Integration with banking systems – Syncs payments directly with records
